title: Outside Time
summary: Daytime outdoor light by morning, peak sun, or afternoon—full sun or shade, with duration—separate from the sunrise practice.

sections.heading: What Outside Time is
sections.body: Outside Time is the daytime outdoor-light habit: you go outdoors after the sunrise slot and practice when, whether you were in full sun or shade, and how long you stayed. It is not the sunrise practice. Sunrise provides the strongest morning-light signal; Outside Time covers the rest of the solar day for skin, spectrum, and place-timed UV.

sections.heading: Why one activity, three slots
sections.body: Morning, peak sun, and afternoon are different jobs. Place sun times help distinguish the timing: morning from sunrise until 1.5 hours before solar noon; peak sun for the symmetrical ±1.5-hour window around solar noon (the UVB-centered band); afternoon from then until sunset. Peak sun is where vitamin D synthesis is most efficient per minute when season allows. Morning and afternoon still train outdoor spectrum and movement—just with different UV profiles.

sections.heading: Practical habit
sections.body: Step outside on purpose. Prefer full sun when safe and non-burning; shade remains useful with less direct exposure. Build duration gradually. Glass does not count as outside. Pair peak-sun practice with the solar-noon vitamin D lesson when repletion is your goal. Repeat the practice when you go out again in a different slot.

sections.heading: What is solid vs framework
sections.body: Solid ground: outdoor daylight differs from indoor LEDs in intensity and spectrum; solar noon UVB matters for vitamin D; non-burning exposure is the safe pattern. Framework: that every shaded minute is worthless, or that Outside Time replaces sunrise eye light. They are complementary—eyes at dawn, skin and day spectrum through Outside Time.

sections.heading: How to use it here
sections.body: Practice Outside Time: choose morning, peak sun, or afternoon, full sun or shaded, and duration. Sunrise practice stays separate. Read Solar noon sun for vitamin D for the peak-sun skin story. Educational only—not dermatology or burn guidance; respect your skin type and clinician advice.
